findings.title: eval_only is ignored when resuming: an evaluate-only run keeps training and overwrites the checkpoint it was asked to evaluate
best_val_loss is overwritten with the latest validation loss whenever always_save_checkpoint is on (the default)
Training runs max_iters + 1 optimizer steps and never evaluates or saves the last one
Command-line values that contain '=' crash the configurator
Imported GPT-2 weights run with exact GELU, but the checkpoints were trained with GPT-2's tanh approximation, so outputs don't match GPT-2
Dataset metadata and config files are loaded as code: meta.pkl is unpickled and config files are exec'd, so a shared dataset folder or config can run arbitrary code
A failed dataset download is cached: a retry skips the download and silently writes an empty dataset
The only checkpoint is overwritten in place, non-atomically: a crash, kill or full disk during torch.save leaves no usable checkpoint
Resume is not exact: RNG and GradScaler state aren't checkpointed, so a resumed run replays the batch sequence from the start of training
Dataset downloads have no timeout and no HTTP status check
train.py is one module-level script whose helpers read globals injected by the exec'd configurator, so no part of the training flow can be imported or tested alone
Config files are exec'd with no key validation: a misspelled setting is silently ignored, while the same typo on the command line is rejected
No type annotations on any function; contracts live in shape comments and bare asserts
Checkpoint keys depend on whether the model was compiled: train.py saves the torch.compile wrapper, so every loader has to strip an '_orig_mod.' prefix it doesn't understand
Tokenizer choice is hard-wired into sample.py: a dataset with any other encoding needs code edits
Leftovers: unoptimized_model is assigned but never used, and GPT.from_pretrained ignores cls
No formatter or linter configured, and small style drifts have crept in
Runtime setup and the training step are copy-pasted across train.py, sample.py and bench.py, and the copies have already drifted
No automated tests at all
Command-line mistakes end in a bare AssertionError with no message, located in '<string>'
Ordering trap: a config file given after a --key=value override silently undoes it
No supported versions stated: no Python version, no tested PyTorch range, no OS matrix
Resuming an interrupted run is undocumented: init_from='resume' appears only in a code comment
Stale or inaccurate statements: 2022 nightly-build advice, bench.py called identical to the training loop, 4 days vs 5 days
No contributor workflow: no contribution guide or agent instructions, no dev setup, and no lint, format or type-check tooling (the missing tests are C4-001)
No CI or automated checks of any kind
No packaged runtime to launch from: each GPU node is set up by hand with an unpinned pip install
Console output is bare print lines: no timestamps, levels or log file, and the learning rate, gradient norm and checkpoint details never reach the console
generate() has no KV cache: every new token re-runs the model over the whole context
bench.py calls CUDA unconditionally, so it fails on CPU and Apple MPS even with --device=cpu
Scripts only run from the repository root: configurator.py and data/ are opened by relative paths
Resume takes the model's shape from the checkpoint but leaves the data loader on the config's block_size, so resuming the README's CPU run with its config crashes
Restarting a run with the same command starts from scratch and overwrites its checkpoint at the first eval, with no warning
A diverged run isn't detected: training continues on NaN loss and, with always_save_checkpoint on (the default), the next eval saves the NaN model over the last good checkpoint
generate() doesn't guard its inputs: temperature 0 (greedy decoding) and an empty prompt both crash
The learning-rate schedule divides by zero when lr_decay_iters equals warmup_iters
.gitignore misses tool outputs the scripts create in the repo root: wandb/ run folders and bench.py's bench_log/ traces
No dependency manifest, pins or lockfile: every install resolves whatever versions are newest that day
Deprecated API: torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler (FutureWarning on every training run)
Gradient-sync skipping toggles DDP's internal require_backward_grad_sync attribute instead of the no_sync() API
The utilisation figure (MFU) assumes an A100 whatever the hardware, and shows -100% for the first iterations
The license isn't declared in any machine-readable metadata, and the repo has no dependency inventory to build an SBOM or license check from
